A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same LanPaint work. Their main text, figures, tables, algorithms, and complete appendices support reliable comparison after matching relocated sections and renumbered displays.

before.justification: V2 reports original Gaussian and Gaussian-mixture sampling experiments, CelebA-HQ and ImageNet benchmarks, component ablations, and production-model image comparisons.

after.justification: V3 retains these original results and adds video demonstrations, alternative-sampler evaluations, expanded step-size results, and a numerical score-approximation check.

M1.justification: The BiG score, FLD dynamics, and Algorithms 1–4 retain the same sampling procedures. The newly named diffusion damping force explains the existing score decomposition. Applying the dimension-independent formulation to video introduces no new algorithmic component.

E1.justification: Section 5.6 and Figure 7 add video inpainting and outpainting, extending evaluation from synthetic distributions and still images to temporally structured clips. Existing image coverage remains. Text, audio, and scientific applications are discussed but not evaluated.

E2.justification: The retained comparisons use the same Replace, CoPaint, DDRM, MCG, DPS, RePaint, and TFG/Langevin comparators. V3 Table 4 varies diffusion samplers across this existing set. MMPS is newly discussed but is not experimentally evaluated.

E3.justification: V3 adds DPM++ Karras and DDIM settings for the existing image comparisons and extends the step-size sweep from 0.05–0.15 to include 0.02 and 0.2. The new video protocol uses 40-frame, 480p clips with a 14B model, 20 Euler steps, and two inner iterations. Existing benchmark sample counts and metrics remain unchanged.

E4.justification: New Table 4 systematically tests dependence on the diffusion sampler across methods and both image datasets. Table 3 extends component ablations to additional step sizes, and Figure 9 investigates the neglected score component underlying the exactness argument. The earlier hyperparameter analysis is retained as Figure 8.

E5.justification: Both versions report benchmark point estimates without introducing confidence intervals, significance tests, or repeated-run aggregation. The production-image examples retain seed 0 and batch size four; the new video examples continue the fixed-seed reporting practice.

E6.justification: Tables 1–2 and retained plots preserve their results. V3 adds substantial sampler-comparison results, additional step-size entries, video outputs, and the score-ratio finding. For example, new Table 4 reports ImageNet LanPaint-10 LPIPS/FID of 0.205/55.1 under DPM++, an additional setting. V2 Figure 16's HiDream portrait comparison is removed.

T1.justification: Theorem 3.1 becomes Theorem 4.1 and changes its remainder from o(sqrt(1-alpha_bar_t)) to O(sqrt(1-alpha_bar_t)), weakening the stated rate while retaining limiting exactness. The underlying assumptions and proofs largely persist. Appendix F, Equation 58, still retains little-o, so the correction is incomplete.

C1.justification: The central claims of training-free, asymptotically exact, efficient conditioning through BiG and FLD remain. Section 4.4 and the closing discussion explicitly broaden the stated applicability to arbitrary-dimensional, non-image modalities, extending the earlier image-focused contribution framing.

C2.justification: V3 explicitly identifies noise-free observations as an applicability restriction and explains that noisy conditioning would require modifying the conditional distribution. It retains the distilled-model limitation while adding proposed distillation directions and broader application discussion. Existing interpretations of the image benchmarks largely remain.

D1.justification: V3 supplies direct LanPaint code and video-example links, whereas v2 only states that a ComfyUI extension was released. It documents the new video's model precision and generation settings and clarifies that the image hyperparameters are shared across tasks without friction fine-tuning. Existing algorithms, hardware information, and mask definitions remain.

R1.justification: V3 adds MMPS discussion, the Wan model citation, and references supporting its broader-impact statement. The main positioning against Langevin, sequential Monte Carlo, and inverse-problem approaches remains. Additional DDIM and DPM-Solver++ bibliography entries concern works already cited in v2.

P1.justification: Related Work moves from Section 5 to Section 2, and implementation details move from Appendix G to Appendix A. V3 polishes grammar and terminology, clarifies conditioning and FLD explanations, and expands the closing sections. Much of the existing prose and appendix exposition is retained.

P2.justification: V3 adds Figures 7 and 9 and the sampler-comparison Table 4, widens Table 3, and introduces table shading. Figure 1 and several appendix comparisons are enlarged and redistributed. The final v2 portrait comparison is removed; retained graphical content is otherwise unchanged.

improvement.justification: The sampler ablations and score-approximation diagnostic strengthen empirical support, while video examples broaden demonstrated applicability. Explicit limitations and direct code links improve interpretation and reuse. These are incremental gains: the main image results remain unchanged, video evidence is qualitative, and the theorem's error-order correction is only partially propagated into Appendix F.
